_comment: On-demand code-navigation MCP servers for Claude Code: the entries that adoption/mcp/claude-user.json and adoption/new-wsl/templates/claude-user.mcp.additions.json carried at user scope until 2026-10-12, unchanged (serena, socraticode, codebase-memory-mcp; semble from the distribution's additions). They are not registered at user scope, so a session starts without their server instructions and tool names. A session that needs them (cross-file refactors, impact analysis, graph questions) loads them for that session only: `claude --mcp-config "$(python3 tools/adoption/install_claude_profile.py --print-mcp-config)"`, which renders ${HOME} and ${ECO_ROOT} for the host; a project can also register one of them with `claude mcp add --scope local`. Subagents inherit the session's servers, so the agents whose tool lists name these tools (evidence-reviewer, isolated-builder, security-reviewer, stack-researcher; the host's codebase-memory, codebase-memory-auditor and codebase-memory-scout) have them in such a session. The placeholders follow the convention of adoption/mcp/claude-user.json, and so do the Claude-side differences from the Codex template. Why and what was measured: docs/decisions/2026-10-12-code-navigation-on-demand.md. jcodemunch is not here: it stays in the user-scope template.
